questions.prompt: Why can count += 1 lose an update when two threads run it?
options: The GIL drops one of them
It's really read, add, write, and the threads can interleave between those steps

questions.prompt: What's the pattern behind most races on shared data? (three words, hyphens allowed)
Race conditions usually show up reliably in testing.
What's the name for code that only one thread may run at a time? (two words)
In Python, what does `with lock:` guarantee when the block raises an exception?
A single lock guards a whole service's state, and throughput stops improving as you add threads. Why?
options: Contention: threads queue on the lock, so the parallel code runs serially

questions.prompt: Which tool lets many readers in at once but only one writer?
Compare-and-swap is an example of what?
options: An atomic operation: a single hardware instruction with no lock
